title: Indonesia's Marathons and Half Marathons Worth the Trip
seo_title: Indonesia's Marathons and Half Marathons Worth the Trip
meta_description: From a World Athletics Gold Label marathon in Jakarta to a half marathon inside a volcanic geopark -- our picks for Indonesia's most worthwhile marathons and half marathons.
dek: Indonesia's race calendar ranges from Jakarta's internationally-recognized flagship marathon to genuinely unusual geopark courses on Java and Sumatra. These are our picks for the country's most worthwhile marathons and half marathons.

sections.heading: Jakarta: The Country's Only World Athletics Gold Label Marathon
paragraphs: The Jakarta Running Festival is the clearest flagship pick in Indonesia -- a World Athletics Gold Label event, the sport's top-tier international certification, with a full spread of distances from 5K to the marathon. That Gold Label status is a genuine, independently verified marker of course measurement accuracy and race organization quality, not just marketing language.

For a runner who wants exactly one Indonesian race that carries real international standing, the Jakarta Running Festival is the clearest answer -- it's the country's benchmark event by that specific, verifiable measure.

sections.heading: Banyuwangi: A Half Marathon Inside a Volcanic Geopark
paragraphs: The Ijen Geopark Run is a genuinely distinctive pick -- a half marathon (with 5K and 10K options) starting at Paltuding Camp in the Kawasan Ijen Geopark, home to the Ijen volcanic crater, one of Indonesia's more striking natural landmarks. This is a course built around a genuinely unusual setting rather than a standard city loop.

Races built around a specific natural landmark like this tend to draw a smaller, more nature-and-adventure-oriented field than a big-city marathon, which is worth factoring in if a quieter, more scenery-focused race day matters more than field size or big-event energy.

sections.heading: Bukittinggi: Sumatra's Own Geopark Race
paragraphs: The Minang Geopark Run, held in Bukittinggi, Sumatera Barat, gives Sumatra its own geopark-style race distinct from Java's Ijen course -- set around the Jam Gadang clock tower and Ngarai Sianok canyon landmarks, both genuinely notable West Sumatran sights. It's a strong pick specifically for a runner who's already covered Java's race scene and wants to see a different Indonesian island.

Like the Ijen race, this is a half-marathon-headlined event with shorter 5K and 10K options, which keeps it accessible to a training group with mixed ability levels rather than requiring everyone to commit to the full half-marathon distance.

sections.heading: Surabaya and Depok: Two Very Different City Race Formats
paragraphs: The Surabaya Orthopedic Half Marathon (SOHM) represents Indonesia's second-largest city's own established half-marathon scene, worth knowing about as an alternative to the more heavily-covered Jakarta calendar. The UI Half Marathon, held on the Universitas Indonesia campus in Depok, is a genuinely different format -- a controlled, campus-based course rather than an open city-street race, which some runners specifically prefer for a calmer, more predictable race environment.
Both are useful additions to a Java-based race trip that wants to go beyond Jakarta without needing to travel to a different island entirely.

faqs.question: Is there a World Athletics Gold Label marathon in Indonesia?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Jakarta Running Festival holds World Athletics Gold Label status, the sport's top-tier international certification for course measurement accuracy and race organization quality. It's Indonesia's clearest benchmark event by that specific, independently verified measure.

faqs.question: Are there unusual, scenic race courses in Indonesia beyond standard city marathons?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Ijen Geopark Run in Banyuwangi starts at the Kawasan Ijen Geopark, home to the striking Ijen volcanic crater, and the Minang Geopark Run in Bukittinggi, Sumatra runs past the Jam Gadang clock tower and Ngarai Sianok canyon. Both are genuinely distinctive alternatives to a standard city-street course.

faqs.question: Is there a good race option in Indonesia outside of Jakarta?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the Surabaya Orthopedic Half Marathon (SOHM) represents Indonesia's second-largest city's own established half-marathon scene, and the Minang Geopark Run gives Sumatra its own distinct race option, both worth considering for a Java or wider-Indonesia trip beyond the capital.
